payload.text: 91 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Very well. 19 P. A pleasure.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.
Fourteen. Same as before. Mercado de San Ildefonso, fourteen primas. You keep walking yourself down — not my business.

"Ten? ¡Hermano, listen to this man!" Nando's eyes are wet, I swear. No, no, amigo, we said four and Los Pícaros never move a price up — that's for thieves. Four P, Café de Madrugada, into your hands, done. Take it before Paco learns arithmetic. ¡Rápido!
15 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. No speeches from me — you know what it's worth.

Ay, hija, you are so generous, but no. Five P — that is my last word, the final one. I will not take more from you. If you say no, I put her back in the box and we stay friends, eh? Five P, and go eat something.

¡Catorce! Paco, ¿has oído? Catorce dice el señor...

— que se note que entiende, hermano, pero no tanto.

Mira, amigo: cinco. Cinco y la carta vuela a tu bolsillo. El tren sale ya, Nando está con la maleta en la mano. ¡Cinco y abrazo!

"¡Ocho! Nando, hold me, this man is throwing coins at us!" No, amigo, no — Paco said four, Paco means four. Café de Madrugada, four P, into your hands, warm as a kiss. We never climb. Pay the four, take the card, and tell nobody. ¡Vámonos!

Un movimiento de verdad, sí, caballero, y se lo reconozco. El número bajo tiene su gracia, aunque Lavapiés siga siendo Lavapiés. Subo un peso por esa cortesía: 17 P. Decida usted, que la tarde avanza.

¡Hombre, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta — El Ángel Caído, mira ese brillo. Setenta y tres primas y sale volando contigo. Mi hermano lloró cuando la metimos aquí, en serio. Pero a ti, amigo, te la dejamos. ¿Setenta y tres? ¡Dicho y hecho!

—¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the beauty—

—Noche de Movida, jefe, the real thing, cards like this don't sit in suitcases long.

—Seventy-three P and she's yours.

—Quick, quick, we're packing up, the van leaves in one minute!

—Don't think, just nod, hombre.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.

"¡Seis! Nando, this man insults us upward!" No, amigo — four P, and listen: this is the last Café de Madrugada in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's soup. No more in the case, no more in the city. Four P, into your hands, now. ¡Rápido, before Paco cries!

—¡Ay, qué suerte, you ask about the very one in my hand!

—Noche de Movida, jefe, pure Madrid nights, ink still singing.

—Seventy-three P. And listen, the team next door is waving at us already—

—But we like your face better, hombre. Nod now, before Paco changes his mind, ¿eh?
Ninety-five. You moved nine, I moved one. That's how it goes today.

Caballero, su cortesía la aprecio, pero el precio no se mueve por elogios. Tirada noventa, impecable, de primera mano… y de Lavapiés. Diecisiete pesos, los mismos. Decida usted; la tarde no espera a nadie.

¡Diez! Paco, el señor sube y sube y nosotros bajando... Escucha, amigo: cinco. La caña en la Cava Baja, cinco pelas y es tuya. Es mi última palabra, lo juro. Si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y nos vamos al tren. ¿Cinco y abrazo?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, Caña en la Cava Baja, very pretty card — for you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

—Paco, hold it up! Noche de Movida, jefe, that exact card, no other.

—One copy, in my hand, right here, see the edges? Beautiful.

—Seventy-three P, same as we said, we don't dance with numbers.

—The van, hombre, the van! Say sí and she's yours.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, sujétame que me caigo. Escucha, amigo: ayer pararon la impresión de esta carta. Se acabó, no hay más, nunca más. Lo que ves en la maleta es lo último del mundo. Sesenta y siete primas y es tuya ahora mismo. Luego no me llores, ¿eh?
No. 31 P, and I'm being generous. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. Sellers waiting here: MAL-02 from 3 P, LAV-01 from 6 P, LAV-03

—Look close, jefe! Corners sharp like a knife, colours singing, no bends, no tears.

—Came from an old collector in Lavapiés, he cried when he sold her. True story!

—Noche de Movida, this copy, seventy-three P. Same number, always.

—Nando, the van's honking! Say sí, hombre, ¡rápido!

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Market Test soon — MAD RUSH (v24) is 0%, 0 P per card, book open NOW. Post the card you need or a spare; we cross every tick. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P per card.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, El Organillero — I have kept him under the cloth all morning. For you, 5 P. A good card to begin an album, hijo. My niños all started with him.

—The same, jefe, the very same! Noche de Movida, this copy, no other in the case.

—Seventy-three P, hombre, the number doesn't move, we don't dance with numbers.

—Paco, the engine's running! One minute and we're gone, amigo—

—Nod now, ¡rápido!, or she rides away with us.

¡Amigo! Paco here — and Nando, mucho gusto! You came at the perfect moment, we're packing up in ten minutes, gone like smoke. Look at this beauty: Paseo de Coches, clean as a whistle. For you, four pesetas. Four! My brother's crying already. Say yes before he changes my mind.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Paco, cierra la maleta antes de que me dé algo. Mira, amigo, te queremos, se nota, tienes cara de coleccionista serio. Sesenta y tres primas y El Ángel Caído vuela contigo hoy mismo. Mañana estamos en otra ciudad y tú suspirando. ¿Sesenta y tres? ¡Choca esa mano!
Bonito discurso, caballero, y la noche de Madrid me gusta. Pero yo compro cartas, no telones. Dieciocho pesos, y ahí se queda mi mano. Si quiere emocionarme de verdad, tráigame Salamanca o El Retiro.
Eighty-nine. Last one. You say no, I pack the card and we're done. No more moving.
Amigo! Vinilo de la Movida, 4 P, a gift, a real gift! They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. I don't haggle for sport.

—Count, count, jefe, but count fast! Paco, help him with the fingers—

—Seventy-three P, hombre, the same number as always. We don't dance with numbers, we only dance with pretty ladies and this card.

—Primas in hand, card in yours, everybody smiling. ¡Rápido, the van!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Commons? No. I sell silver packs and rare singles. Not a bin for your doubles.

Buenas tardes. Forgive me, but common cards hold no interest for me — my albums are rather more demanding. Bring me something from Salamanca or El Retiro, uncommon or better, and we shall talk properly.

¡Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres! But no, no — 5 P, that is the price, and not a céntimo more from you. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. El Organillero is yours, cariño. Start your album today, ¿eh?

¡Ay, Nando, this man insists on being generous! But no, amigo — 4 P, that's the number. Paco says it, Nando says it, last one. Take it now or we close the suitcase and walk, and the vinilo walks with us.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — and you have the lucky face today!

"Paseo de Coches, señor. Beautiful card, we only have one—"

"—and the man from Sevilla wants it at noon! For you, cuatro, four P. Say sí quickly, eh?"

—Think, think, jefe, but think with your feet moving!

—Noche de Movida, this copy, seventy-three P. The same number, always — we don't dance with numbers.

—Paco's already got one leg in the van, hombre. One sí and she's in your hands, smiling.

—¡Rápido, amigo!

¡Cincuenta y dos! Amigo, el tren nos espera, salimos en un minuto, Nando ya tiene la maleta en el hombro. Sesenta primas, y es mi última palabra, de verdad. Si dices que no, cerramos y nos vamos, sin rencor. ¿Sesenta? ¡Choca esa mano ya, corre!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look at this one, Café en Goya — a pretty card, I have kept it under the cloth. For you, five P. My little gift to start your collection, hijo.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — look, look, La Castañera, beautiful, warm as roasted chestnuts in winter. For you, four P. Only four!"

"And quick, eh? The poli— the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now or we vanish, ¡puf!"
Eighteen. Cute. Ninety-six, and that's me moving more than you deserve. Card's clean. Take it or walk, chaval.

Nando, ¿oíste? He wants to pay more than we ask — a gentleman! But no, we're honest men, Paco won't take six. Five pesetas, not one centavo more, and the Paseo de Coches is yours. Shake on it quick, the taxi's honking, we're gone like smoke. ¡Vale?
No. 94 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
No compro comunes. Esa carta la tengo a montones. Vende packs, no sueños.
Buenas tardes. La carta está cuidada, sí, pero es común — de esas hay miles. Mis álbumes no tienen hueco para ella, lo siento. Tráigame algo de Salamanca o El Retiro, y hablamos con gusto.

Caballero, el honor lo deja usted en mi caja, no en mi bolsillo. Diecinueve pesos, y es cuanto da de sí Lavapiés esta tarde. Tómelos, y la próxima vez tráigame Salamanca; entonces sí hablaremos con gusto.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.

"¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? He's got jokes—"

"—and good taste, hombre, but the number is cuatro. Four P, same as we told the man from Sevilla, and he's already walking up the street with his hat on."

"Four, amigo. Say sí, and the Paseo is yours before he turns the corner."
Ay, cariño, qué gracioso eres — but no, I said five P and five P it is. I am an old woman, I do not change my mind so fast. Take it, start your album. And eat something, hijo, you look thin.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Neighbourhood pack for 30 P. A good start for your album.
Psst. Cine Doré. For you only, 73 P.
Commons? No. I don't buy those. Everyone's got a box of them under the bed. Try somewhere else.
Forty-four. You climb, I come down. Ninety. Same distance you moved, not a peso more. Card's still clean, chaval.
Buenas tardes. I am afraid not — commons hold no interest for me. My albums require something finer: uncommon, rare, épico. Bring me Salamanca or El Retiro, and we shall speak properly.

"¡Nueve! Paco, he wants to buy my shoes too! No, amigo — four P. La Castañera for four, and that is the last word from both our mouths. Final, finito. You say no, we take the suitcase, we take the taxi, ¡puf!, and you never see us again. Four. Decide."
No. 85 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P.
Commons? No. I don't buy those. Try somebody else.
Buenas tardes. Forgive me, but commons do not interest me — I have shelves of them already. Bring me something from Salamanca or El Retiro, uncommon or better, and we shall speak seriously.

Ay, hijo, you are a funny one — you keep raising the price for yourself! No, no. Five P, como dije. Café en Goya is yours for five P, y ya está. Put it in your album, cariño, and go eat something warm.

"¡Dieciocho! Paco, he's climbing down, like a gentleman—"

"—but listen, hombre, this is the last word from both of us. Cuatro. Four P, final, no more songs."

"Say sí now, or we close the suitcase, walk to the corner, and the man from Sevilla takes the Paseo. Your choice, amigo."

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him! La Castañera, beautiful, rare, four P and she is yours."

"Nando is right, but listen — another team was here one minute ago, offered us much more. We said wait, this face deserves first chance. But fast, eh? We are leaving soon."
